rtbeat sidecar** (see _Owner stamp & heartbeat_) — `owner.last_heartbeat` itself is the run-start stamp, not a live-advancing field:
  - `status` — `"running"` while the orchestrator holds the run; `"done"` once `faff run close` runs (every exit path), except that a sentry abort's `"aborted-resumable"` is kept.
  - `pid` — the orchestrator's process id (same-host best-effort liveness corroborator; may be omitted).
  - `session_id` — the owning-session token (use the `<run-id>`); paired with the `FAFF_RUN_DIR` export below it lets a session recognise its **own** run.
  - `started_at` / `last_heartbeat` — ISO-8601, both written once at run start. `owner.last_heartbeat` is the run-start baseline (and the legacy/overlay fallback for a legacy ledger with no sidecar); the sidecar file is what advances each tick (see _Owner stamp & heartbeat_). `harness` / `model` (additive) come from the same resolver every durable artifact reads; absent on an older ledger — legacy/unowned, never depended on. `faff_version` (additive) is written by the CLI mint, never by prose; absent on an older ledger.

### Owner stamp & heartbeat

- **At run start** (before step 4), capture `measure_root=$PWD` (before any worktree work) and `session_id=$CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID` — every later token call passes them as `--root "$measure_root" --session-id "$session_id"` — then call `run open` and branch on its exit before evaluating anything:

  ```bash
  out=$("$faff" run open --mode <mode> [--until HH:MM] [--max N] --root "$measure_root" --session-id "$session_id" --export); rc=$?
  [ "$rc" -eq 2 ] || eval "$out"   # exports FAFF_RUN_DIR and FAFF_SESSION_ID, so this session's Stop hook recognises its run
  ```

  A run minted by `faff lights-out` passes `--adopt-run-dir "$FAFF_RUN_DIR"` in place of `--mode` and no `--until`/`--max`. `run open` mints or adopts the run, fills `owner.harness`/`model`, writes the budget envelope once and the `budget baseline`, settles Commissaire governance (admit, `admit-required`, the fail-closed paths) through its existing verbs, runs `hooks-ensure`, then starts the sentry poller — which only acts on an unattended run. §0a's `inherited-l4` reuse never calls it. Route on `rc`:

  | `rc` | Action |
  |---|---|
  | `0` | Proceed to step 4. Relay the `hooks-ensure:` line `run open` prints on stderr to the user when it says hooks were added. |
  | `3` | Governance failed closed: `run open` already appended `run-end` (`governance-admit-failed`) and closed the owner, and no build starts. On an adopted run that already had admitted work, run `faff runcheck "$FAFF_RUN_DIR" --json` and park each issue in its `undispatched` per the shared protocol (cause `governance-admit-failed`), so the done run trips no Stop hook. Then go to `## Reporting` (`run summary`); do not call `run close`. |
  | `2`, or unparseable output | Log it and park per the shared protocol, as a mint failure; dispatch nothing. |
- **Refresh the heartbeat across the WHOLE graft lifecycle, not just at issue boundaries — via `faff heartbeat`, never a hand-rolled ledger edit.** Run `faff heartbeat "$FAFF_RUN_DIR"` at every wave/issue boundary. A tick's only write is the dedicated single-value file `<run-dir>/heartbeat` (atomic tmp + rename) — it never touches the run ledger. This is what structurally closes the concurrent-outcome-write race the old ledger field-merge could only narrow: a single-value tmp+rename file cannot be clobbered by a whole-file ledger write, so there is no interleaving for a tick and an outcome write to lose. The slow phases now run **inside the dispatched build subagent**, which ticks `faff heartbeat` from inside its own long sub-steps (faff-graft Step 7.5 / Step 9) — the orchestrator forwards `run_dir` in the `BuildDispatch` so the subagent resolves the owning ledger deterministically. A boundary-only refresh would let the heartbeat go stale mid-review and false-block again; the default staleness threshold is 900s (`FAFF_RUN_HEARTBEAT_STALE_SECS`) and a single review step can approach it. This is the load-bearing reason liveness is owner-emitted, never inferred from worktree mtimes (a quiet worktree mid-review is *normal in-flight*, not stalled).
- **At orchestrator exit** (every path but a fail-closed `run open`, whose exit 3 already appended `run-end` and closed the owner), after step 11.6 and before `run summary`, synchronously in-turn (step 11.6 → **Run-end synchronicity invariant**):

  ```bash
  "$faff" run close --run-dir "$FAFF_RUN_DIR" --stop-reason <the summary's Stop reason token> [--git-only] --root "$measure_root" --session-id "$session_id" --json
  ```

  It refuses (exit 3, nothing written) while an admitted issue has no outcome, except a `sentry-abort` close of a run carrying the abort mark, which reports the resume's work in `undispatched`. Otherwise it appends the `run-end` event, writes `stop_reason` and the owner close in one locked edit, stops the poller, reconciles and concludes each admitted issue on a governed run, mints the git-only run-level anchor and run-close bundle (`--git-only` is step 8.5's once-resolved signal), mints the judge trail and pumps andon (never `audit seal`: bundle publish already seals); a failed step is a fault and the close proceeds. `0` → `## Reporting`; `3` → step 11's dispatch-or-park for `undispatched`, then close again; `2` → log and surface needs-human.

The hook reads this owner record but **never writes it** — only the run's own agents (the orchestrator and its dispatched build subagents) write it, and only via `faff heartbeat`, which writes the heartbeat sidecar, never the owner block (the close at exit is `faff run close`'s one locked edit). Liveness is on-disk owner-emitted state, never a tracker read, network call, or foreign-pid probe (the pure-function CLI invariant).

### Stop hook (harness-enforced backstop)
